newsitem.title: MEXICO: San Luis eyes $15 mln gold investment.
newsitem.headline: San Luis eyes $15 mln gold investment.

text.p: Corporacion Industrial San Luis is weighing a $10-$15 million investment in a gold mining project in the Asientos area of the central state of Aguascalientes, the company chairman said at a news conference on Thursday.

"It's a gold project which we hope to ratify in the next six months, that would require investment of the order of $10 million, $15 million in its first phase," said Antonio Madero Bracho, San Luis chairman.
"We have a growth plan to triple the size of the company over the next two years, mainly in autoparts, but we will also make sizeable investments in mining."
Madero said Asientos area had potential in gold, zinc and copper deposits. Gold ore deposits in the Asientos area totalled 12,000 tonnes, but with only one gram of gold per tonne of ore.
"Commercialy exportable deposits currently have three to four grams (of gold) per tonne, but there is technology to make the deposits economically viable," he said.
Copper and zinc mining projects were more long term and deposits were still under investigation.
"I believe we have about eight million tonnes, but it's early days yet," Madero added.
